notice: Hand-authored observation, probabilities and sampling draws. Not captured gameplay, real model inference or an executed command. Refs are illustrative.
observationPolicy: HUD/inventory/scoreboard and own grounded/water/motion feedback; renderer-labelled final visible pixels, surface appearance and current animation; captions from nonzero spatialized sound samples; bounded memories of actual observations/actions. Not RGB/audio recognition. No world coordinates, metric ranges, hidden entities, future states or route/LOS probes. Labels can exceed human recognition in darkness; current animation uses fingerprinted asset labels or meaningful frame names; unknown appearances abstain. Every question includes the same complete HUD-owned weapon inventory and ammo pools, separate from the actual held weapon. Pickups/ammunition do not imply ownership. Weapon reach, relative strength and switch-ammo requirements are static game knowledge, not measured target distance. Brush door/button functions are not revealed by server class. Opaque execution references expire on visual loss; they are not tracking identities.
controller: The model selects a tactic and its visible target/item, plus a concurrent owned-weapon choice, through explicit questions. Each used choice head is sampled once from its full public probability distribution (temperature 1, no top-k/p); only rounding is normalized. Best-effective-loaded-gun guidance and an axe-last-resort preference are prompt instructions, not a fixed ranking or sampling exemption for weapons. Raw SDK top choices and probabilities remain unchanged. Every draw, interval and option order is recorded; rejected decisions are never resampled. The separate noul diagnostic ranks independent ratings, which are not categorical probabilities. Code only executes that composite choice: bounded relative movement, visible-pixel aim, aim-overlap attack input, one jump press, or swim input. The explicit Engage goal additionally advances while the current HUD weapon is the axe; a ranged weapon attacks without that advance. This is declared goal execution, never an override of Hold position or raw attacks. It does not measure reach or find a route; normal collisions may block it. Keeping a weapon never spends an action; a different one gets a single switch press, with firing suppressed for that press only. Normal game weapon refusal/fallback must not deadlock a chosen attack. No tactical shortlist, danger/ammo veto, target substitution, hidden tracking or pathfinding. Visual loss or a visible death/corpse pose stops that targeted attack, without choosing a replacement. Downed/recovering zombies are not declared dead. Releasing pixel aim or finishing an explicit model look-up/down command returns pitch toward level at up to 180 degrees/second, for at most 30 ticks or 750ms; no yaw, movement, attack or retargeting is added. A new target or active explicit look-up/down takes priority; only executed camera input owes later leveling. Stop suspends cleanup and frozen Step never advances extra frames; ordinary subsequent commands can finish leveling. Normal Quake physics, weapon rules and damage apply.

notes: All tactics are offered without geometry probes, resource/health filtering or a tactical shortlist.
Separate choice questions share the same state in one batch. The chosen tactic's target and the concurrent weapon choice are used. Keeping the shotgun does not consume a separate action.
Full distributions are sampled once, in offer order. Each used head records its draw and interval; the original SDK argmax and probabilities remain untouched. No retry or tactical substitution.
Here the illustrative action draw selects Engage rather than the SDK's top back-fire; the aim and equipment draws choose e1 and shotgun.
Visible lava coverage is not a predicted movement outcome. There is no hit, safety or collection guarantee.
